basic_info.name: Fellowship.xyz
basic_info.location: London (HQ), Los Angeles, Marrakech, Sardinia (no permanent exhibition space -- operates across locations and online)

practice_description.medium: Gallery, publishing, curation, online exhibitions, AI video, photography, digital art
practice_description.practice_summary: Contemporary art gallery canonising AI and algorithmic art, representing defining digital artists and operating the Daily Program -- a year-long curatorial initiative documenting the evolution of AI art through daily commissions from 137+ artists producing 3,500+ works.
practice_description.methodology: Fellowship operates without a permanent physical space, instead curating exhibitions across multiple cities and online. Their approach combines institutional-level curation with Web3 infrastructure (smart contracts, blockchain provenance). The Daily Program commissions artists to create new works daily, building a comprehensive visual timeline of AI art evolution. They also publish large-format books (alignDRAW 10th anniversary) with critical essays positioning computational creation within art history. Co-founded by Alejandro Cartagena and Chadwick Tyler, with founding involvement from Holly Hay (Wallpaper photography director).

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Fellowship is actively building the canon of AI/algorithmic art and representing key practitioners (Herndon/Dryhurst). Their Daily Program creates a living archive of AI art evolution that could serve as source material for a graph-curated exhibition, and their institutional placement work connects digital art to museum collections.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Indirectly. Fellowship's Daily Program archive (3,500+ AI artworks) could function as a rich substrate dataset for generative composition. The gallery's curatorial framing positions AI art as a coherent body of work with internal relationships.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. The Daily Program is inherently relational -- 137 artists contributing to a shared smart contract, with works positioned in relation to each other as a collective timeline. The program encourages artists to share processes and inspirations, building visible connections.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: The Daily Program accumulates daily, creating an ever-growing archive. Season 2 builds on Season 1's foundation. The archive itself is a continuously expanding composition.

works.title: Daily Program Season 1
works.description: Year-long curatorial initiative dedicated to AI video, featuring 137 artists creating 3,500+ unique works documenting the medium's evolution from SORA to text-to-story narratives. Artists contribute to a shared collection and smart contract.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how a curatorial structure can produce a living, relational archive of AI art -- a model for A(DAI)'s graph-based approach to field intelligence.

works.title: alignDRAW 10th Anniversary (2015-2025)
works.description: Large-format book celebrating Elman Mansimov's 2015 alignDRAW -- the first text-to-image AI system. Includes essays by Lev Manovich, Shana Lopes, Eva Jager, Mat Dryhurst, and Darius Himes, plus interview film and new model outputs.
works.relevance: Positions computational research as art historical event. Mat Dryhurst's essay argues that arXiv and engineering communities are where 'glimpses of the world to come' emerge -- aligning with A(DAI)'s interest in field intelligence from unconventional sources.

works.title: Infinite Images by Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst
works.description: Exhibition by Herndon and Dryhurst hosted on Fellowship's platform, connecting their AI art practice to the gallery's broader curatorial program.
works.relevance: Direct connection between Fellowship's roster and A(DAI)'s key practitioners.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Fellowship designs curatorial protocols (Daily Program structure, shared smart contracts, artist-trading editions) that shape how AI art is produced, collected, and historically positioned. The gallery itself functions as infrastructure for canonisation.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: The Daily Program smart contract system where 137 artists contribute to a shared collection; the alignDRAW canonisation project positioning research outputs as art; institutional placement pipeline connecting digital art to MoMA, LACMA, ZKM collections [uncertain].

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Fellowship operates commercially but with community-oriented structures. The Daily Program's shared smart contract creates collective ownership among artists. The gallery's emphasis on transparency (artists sharing processes) and community building aligns with commons principles, though it operates as a commercial gallery.

governance_model.governance_detail: Gallery-led curation with strong artist input. Co-founders Alejandro Cartagena and Chadwick Tyler lead curatorial direction. The Daily Program involves invited curators and artist self-direction within the program's framework. Smart contract structures automate certain governance functions (revenue sharing, edition management).

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Artists participate by invitation and consent to the shared smart contract and exhibition terms. Blockchain provenance ensures clear attribution.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Individual artists create works, but the Daily Program positions them within a collective frame. The shared smart contract creates a form of collective authorship at the program level while preserving individual artist identity.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: The Daily Program produces new artworks every day, building an ever-growing archive. Seasons structure the accumulation (Season 1: AI video; Season 2: emerging artists). The gallery's exhibition program evolves across locations and online.

data_materiality.data_sources: AI-generated artworks (video, image) from 137+ artists, curatorial metadata, blockchain transaction records, critical essays and interviews, recording of AI art's historical evolution.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Artist-generated. Each work is created by an invited artist using their own tools and processes. Blockchain provides provenance records. The alignDRAW project explicitly traces the provenance of the first text-to-image system.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Fellowship's artists work extensively with AI embedding spaces (text-to-image, text-to-video models). The Daily Program archive implicitly maps the evolution of these embedding spaces over time as AI tools advance.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. The gallery spans AI video, AI image generation, photography, print publishing, and online exhibitions.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: No permanent physical space. Exhibitions manifest across London, LA, Marrakech, and Sardinia venues, plus online platform (fellowship.xyz, daily.xyz). The lack of fixed space is itself a curatorial statement -- the gallery exists as a network.

interoperability.composability: The Daily Program's shared smart contract creates interoperable ownership records. The online platform (daily.xyz) provides accessible exhibition infrastructure. Published essays and catalogues create textual connections to broader discourse.
interoperability.technical_openness: Hybrid. Blockchain-based provenance is transparent, but the gallery operates commercially. Smart contracts provide some programmable openness.

technical_approach.stack: Blockchain smart contracts (likely Ethereum/Tezos), Web3 exhibition platform (fellowship.xyz, daily.xyz), digital publishing, AI art tools (varied by artist -- SORA, Stable Diffusion, custom models, etc.)

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art, algorithmic art, digital photography, Web3 art market, institutional art world (Art Basel participation), academic/critical discourse (Lev Manovich, Eva Jager connections)
network_position.connections: Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst (represented artists), Serpentine Arts Technologies (Eva Jager contributes essays), Feral File (parallel platform in digital art space, Herndon/Dryhurst exhibited on both), MoMA (institutional placements [uncertain]), LACMA (institutional placements [uncertain]), ZKM (Mat Dryhurst connection), alignDRAW/Elman Mansimov (canonisation project)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Fellowship's Daily Program archive, artist network, and canonisation methodology are directly valuable to A(DAI). The gallery represents key practitioners (Herndon/Dryhurst) and is building the institutional framework for AI art's historical positioning. Partnership could provide A(DAI) with access to practitioner networks, curatorial intelligence, and the Daily Program's structured archive of AI art evolution.
